scope: Theorem 1.2 (Termination of ordinary programs) of the manuscript “Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds” (preprints/Finite-ordinary-minimal-model-programs-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 056 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1b9511572d6c717), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 2-3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Let X be a normal globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold, with a canonical Weil divisor KX, and let ∆ ≥ 0 be a rational divisor such that (X, ∆) is klt. Then every maximal ordinary negative-ray program starting on (X, ∆) terminates. Its birational steps form a finite sequence (X, ∆) = (X0, ∆0) 99K · · · 99K (Xn, ∆n). Every Xi is normal, compact Kähler and globally Weil Q-factorial; every (Xi, ∆i) is klt, and Di = KXi + ∆i is Q-Cartier. The canonical divisors are the transforms of the specified datum. The following alternatives hold. (i) If D = KX + ∆ is pseudo-effective, then Dn is nef. The composite ϕ : X 99K Xn extracts no prime divisor, and a(E; X, ∆) ≤ a(E; Xn, ∆n) for every prime divisor over the two models, with strict inequality for every prime on X contracted by ϕ. MINIMAL MODEL PROGRAMS ON KÄHLER FOURFOLDS 3 (ii) If D is not pseudo-effective, there is a projective surjective morphism g : Xn → S with connected fibres, where S is normal compact Kähler, dim S < 4, ρ(Xn/S) = 1, and −Dn is g-ample. For each negative contraction, including g, the relative Bott–Chern dimension is one. If X is globally strongly Q-factorial, so is every Xi. The same conclusions hold in the intrinsic formulation with the canonical rational line bundle in place of a chosen canonical Weil divisor. In either formulation the first model is exactly X.
